cases.why: The mockup's trio. Slot 1 = best FREE action = keep-leaf-cover (covers food+shelter, the most). Then add-water-source (water), then plant-native-shrub (nesting, ahead of mark-windows on priority 3 vs 2). Spicebush needs shade/partial so it fits; red cedar is full-sun only so it is hidden (1).

Regression for the critic's finding: a cavity nester in January must be shown the nest box even with several free actions eligible. Slot 1 = free keep-leaf-cover; slot 2 = add-nest-box (it covers nesting and is featured for the chickadee, worth +2); slot 3 = add-water-source (water, still uncovered). Safety has no remedy in January (mark-windows is off-season): unmet.

leave-dead-wood is for dowwoo, featured for it, and covers food+shelter+nesting, so it is the free first step. add-water-source covers water. After that no remaining action covers a new need (safety has nothing in January), so only TWO actions are shown: no padding with keep-leaf-cover. White oak is full-sun only so it is hidden for partial sun.

Hummingbird has no water need, so water actions cover nothing; the only food action in July for balcony/containers is skip-pesticides. After it, nothing covers a new need, so ONE action is shown. Nothing in a container setup addresses shelter, nesting or safety in July: unmet. Both red tubular flowers tie at 30 (cardinal-flower before trumpet-honeysuckle by id).

Unknown species (null birdId): generic advice, bird-specific actions (nest box, dead wood) excluded, every need type counts equally, so the same three as the cardinal. Plants rank by breadth (sum of link weights over all birds): serviceberry 8, dogwood 7, arrowwood 6 = creeper 6, ... Full-sun-only plants (white oak, red cedar, coneflower, aster) are hidden: 4. black-chokeberry has no links so it never appears.

Budget 'free': free actions only, and no plants at all, so all 6 linked plants count as hidden. After leaf cover (food, shelter) and water, no FREE action covers a new need, so two actions are shown. Nesting and safety have no free remedy, but a small budget would unlock plant-native-shrub and mark-windows (moreBudget): the UI must say that, not 'nothing can help'.

Balcony: yard-only actions drop out. leave-seed-heads is the goldfinch's signature action (featured, +2) and free, so it is the free first step. Then add-water-source (water), then mark-windows (safety). Shelter and nesting have no balcony remedy: unmet. New England aster is yard-only: hidden (1).

Edge case: deep shade. Every plant linked to the titmouse (white oak, dogwood, serviceberry) needs sun, so the plant list is empty and all 3 are reported hidden; the UI must say 'no plant fits this sun'. Actions are unaffected by sun.

Journal rule. Without a journal the two weight-3 plants order by id: common-winterberry then serviceberry. With norcar and bkcchi in the journal, serviceberry also helps bkcchi (+1 = 31) so it moves ahead; holly and dogwood each also help norcar (+1 = 21). Creeper stays 20. June: add-water-source (water) and skip-pesticides (food); the birdbath-scrubbing action would only repeat water, so it is not shown. Nesting and safety have no remedy now.
Nuthatch gets leave-dead-wood (food+shelter+nesting) as slot 1, then water, then mark-windows (safety, in season in November). Only one plant is linked (white oak, full sun).

March, Carolina Wren, everything in season. Slot 1 = free keep-leaf-cover. Slot 2 = add-nest-box: it covers nesting and is featured for the wren (+2), so it beats plant-native-shrub, which would also cover nesting. Slot 3 = add-water-source. (Before the 'featured' rule the shrub took slot 2 and the nest box was never shown.)

Season rule: in January plant-native-shrub is out of season and must not appear. Only leaf cover and water add a need, so two actions are shown (brush pile and seed heads would repeat covered needs). Nesting has a plant remedy (arrowwood viburnum fits full sun) so it is not unmet; safety has none this month. Dogwood and spicebush need partial sun or shade: hidden (2).

Generic mode with a journal of goldfinch + hummingbird. Actions: water, then skip-pesticides (food); scrubbing the birdbath would repeat water, so it is not shown. Journal adds +1 for each journal bird a plant helps: black-eyed-susan 5->6, purple-coneflower 4->6 (helps both), aster 3->4, honeysuckle 3->4, cardinal-flower 3->4. White oak (16) and serviceberry (8) still lead. 12 plants fit full-sun yard; dogwood and spicebush are hidden.

Worst case for a nuthatch: balcony, shade. The only linked plant (white oak) needs full sun: none shown, 1 hidden. Balcony offers water, pesticide-free and window actions only; shelter and nesting are unmet.
Month 0 is a programming error, never silently clamped.
Month 13 is a programming error.
A birdId that is not in the content is a bug in the caller (an unresolved species is null, not a made-up id).
Content covers us-ne only. Any other region code must fail loudly rather than return Northeast advice for a Colorado yard. The UI maps a state (NJ) to us-ne before calling.

The journal comes from stored sightings and may hold ids from older content. An unknown journal id is ignored, never an error: same result as with an empty journal. The goldfinch's signature action leave-seed-heads (featured) now takes the free first slot; plant-native-shrub covers shelter and nesting (2 new needs); add-water-source covers water.

Generic + free + balcony + January: only two actions are possible at all (add-water-source, leave-seed-heads), so fewer than three are returned. No plants on a free budget; all 14 linked plants are reported hidden.

Hummingbird again, now in a yard in September. No water need, so no water action is chosen: keep-leaf-cover (food+shelter), then plant-native-shrub (nesting, ahead of mark-windows on id order of equal gain), then mark-windows (safety). Purple coneflower is full-sun only: hidden (1).
